facts.claim: Chasepoint sells goods and services to travellers.
Chasepoint gathers or works a resource the player can see.
A player can buy and sell at Chasepoint.
Goods are stored at Chasepoint for a player to find.
Chasepoint is an Imperial road stage east of Soulrest.
The Legion built the stage.
The wreck-salvage families keep the stage.
Chasepoint stands on the last firm ground before the coast road turns inland.
Wreckage from the Southern Sea comes ashore on the coast to the south.
Salvage rights are hereditary here and closely guarded.
The stage's old stable now dries the recovered rope and cordage.
No stage-keeper has been paid in two centuries.
The roof is Argonian reed thatch on Imperial walls.
The yard is stacked with ships' timber cut in other provinces.
The way-station has a straight ridge and a square yard wall.
The walls are Imperial grey plaster over a rubble core.
The families here call the thatched roof a bodge.
A salvage stall sells goods recovered from wrecks in the past week.
A salvage lot can be traced to a ship whose owners do not know it sank.
A locked chest beside the old stable holds salvage held back from the count.
The square yard wall reads through scrub from the road bend.
The reed roof over the wall names the current occupants.
The place is sound but scavenged: the pantiles are gone and the roof is replaced with what grows here.
The rest is Imperial and holding.
The mood is thrifty and proprietorial.
The colours are grey plaster, rubble stone and bleached driftwood.
There is road traffic, and the sea two fields away, out of sight.
There is wet plaster, and tar from the timber stacks.
A revived coast road with paid stage-keepers would make it a proper town again.
